thought.text: Java 21 installed. The earlier pnpm install process — let me check its final state, then re-run install (now that Java exists, `prepare` should work; store is already warm).

reasoning_content:
Java 21 is already installed. Next, re-run pnpm install (the package downloads are already cached in the store, so this should be fast). However, the `prepare` step requires Java and will take a long time to generate the API client.

Also, the pnpm install I ran earlier may still be "RUNNING" (according to pgrep). I'll check and either terminate it or wait for it. In reality, the last pgrep displayed RUNNING, but this may be a stale process, or a hung process. First I'll check the log, and then re-run pnpm install.

action.command: tail -3 /tmp/pnpm-install.log; echo "=== process ==="; pgrep -f "pnpm install" >/dev/null && echo RUNNING || echo DONE; pkill -f "pnpm install" 2>/dev/null; sleep 2; pgrep -f "pnpm install" >/dev/null && echo STILL || echo KILLED

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "tail -3 /tmp/pnpm-install.log; echo \"=== process ===\"; pgrep -f \"pnpm install\" >/dev/null && echo RUNNING || echo DONE; pkill -f \"pnpm install\" 2>/dev/null; sleep 2; pgrep -f \"pnpm install\" >/dev/null && echo STILL || echo KILLED", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Check and stop stale pnpm install process"}
